title: Geometric fibre cardinality of a separated etale morphism does not increase under specialization
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact separated etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For a specialization of geometric points $\bar y_{\mathrm{gen}}\leadsto\bar y_{\mathrm{sp}}$ [def-weil-geometric-point] of $Y$, the geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] over $\bar y_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is finite whenever the geometric fibre over $\bar y_{\mathrm{gen}}$ is finite, and its cardinality is at most that of the geometric fibre over $\bar y_{\mathrm{gen}}$. In particular, if the geometric fibres over a dense open have cardinality strictly less than an integer $d$, then every geometric fibre has cardinality strictly less than $d$.

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), induction step: specialization of separated etale fibres preserves the strict bound

proof.text: Work over an affine open of $Y$ containing the image of the specialization. The etale morphism is flat and locally of finite presentation, and its separated quasi-compact restriction is quasi-finite; hence the restriction satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-qf-stratification].

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), induction proof, using Lemma 07RZ after restricting to an affine open

proof.text: Let $\emptyset=Z_{-1}\subseteq Z_0\subseteq\cdots$ and $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ be the stratification supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fp-qf-stratification]. Applying its universal property to $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ shows that the fibre over $y$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ exactly when $y\in S_r$. The fibre $X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and finite, hence $X_y=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is affine. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], such an etale fibre algebra $C$ is a finite product of finite separable field extensions, so this degree is the number of geometric points in the fibre. Consequently the locus where the geometric fibre has cardinality at most $r$ is the closed set $Z_r$.

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), induction proof: apply Lemma 07RZ to the residue-field point and use the etale-over-a-field decomposition

proof.text: If $\bar y_{\mathrm{gen}}\leadsto\bar y_{\mathrm{sp}}$ lies over $y_{\mathrm{gen}}\leadsto y_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the generic fibre has finite cardinality $r$, then $y_{\mathrm{gen}}\in Z_r$. Since $Z_r$ is closed and closed sets are stable under specialization, $y_{\mathrm{sp}}\in Z_r$, proving that the special fibre is finite with cardinality at most that of the generic fibre.

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), conclusion of the specialization argument

proof.text: For the strict-bound clause, on each affine open the closed set $Z_{d-1}$ contains the dense open locus where the fibre cardinality is less than $d$. Therefore it equals the whole affine open, and these local conclusions cover $Y$; every geometric fibre has cardinality strictly less than $d$.

source.place: Lemma 37.45.7 (Tag 09Z0), strict-bound conclusion via the closed stratum $Z_{d-1}$
